onboarding.title: First run
onboarding.welcome.title: What Tempience is
onboarding.welcome.p1: Tempience is a notebook with a line of time instead of pages. Every record knows when it happened or when it is meant to happen. Each one relates to something — a person, a place, a piece of work. And each can be linked to others. That is how separate notes become one story: plans next to what actually came of them, today next to what came before.
onboarding.welcome.p2: Three words you will meet everywhere: **Trace** — a record. **Scope** — the context a record belongs to. **Intersection** — a link that makes a record part of something bigger.
onboarding.trace.title: Trace
onboarding.trace.p1: A Trace is one record: something that happened, or something you intend to do. “Signed the contract.” “Call Mum.” “I think we went to the seaside in spring 2019.” Tempience does not ask whether this is a diary or a plan: a record has two states — an **intention** and **what happened**. An intention can later be confirmed by what happened — and you can see what came of what you planned.
onboarding.trace.p2: Every Trace stands on the line of time, but the time does not have to be exact. “14:30” — exact. “In March” — to the month. “In summer, roughly” — approximate. “A week after the move” — relative to another record. “I don't remember when” — that works too: the record waits until the time turns up.
onboarding.trace.p3: **Kind.** Some records repeat and consist of numbers: weight, a run, the electricity bill. For those there is Kind — a type of record with its own form. You describe the fields once (“Run: kilometres, minutes”), then only enter values. Such a record has no title — the values are the record, and all records of one Kind open as a table: a history by date.
onboarding.scope.title: Scope
onboarding.scope.p1: A Scope is the context in which a record makes sense: a person, a place, a project, a topic, a habit. “Work”, “Anya”, “The flat”, “Spanish”. A record can be put into one Scope, into several, or into none. Scopes form a tree — “Health → Running”, “Work → Studio” — and everything inside is visible at the parent. There is one tree, and it is yours: not a classification of life, but a convenient map. Next to the name there is a note — for what is not tied to a date.
onboarding.links.title: Links and Period
onboarding.links.p1: A link is what turns records into a story. Writing down “the kettle broke” is easy. The interesting part is elsewhere: the kettle broke *a week after the move* — one record's time through another's. “Buy a kettle” is *part of the whole* “Set up the kitchen”. “Bought a kettle” is a *confirmation* that the intention was carried out. A note six months later, “that kettle really was bad”, is a *return* to the old record.
onboarding.links.p2: Kinds of links: **Belonging** — a Trace belongs to a Scope. **Nested Scope** — a Scope inside a Scope. **Part of the whole** — a step inside a bigger undertaking. **Confirmation** — what happened answers an intention. **Return** — a new record refines, corrects or comments on an old one. **Related** — simply side by side, with no hierarchy.
onboarding.links.p3: No link is required. But each one makes a thought stop being a lonely line and become part of the flow.
onboarding.links.p4: **Period** — a stretch of the calendar: a day, a week, a month, a year, a decade. Choose one on the axis and you see everything that fell into it, and which Scopes were active at the time. Nothing needs to be put into a Period: records land there on their own, by time. And about a period as a whole you can leave one note — the month's summary, a thought about the year.
onboarding.try.title: Try it
onboarding.try.demo.title: Dr. Watson's notebook
onboarding.try.demo.body: 1881–1894: meeting Holmes, “The Speckled Band”, “The Hound of the Baskervilles”, Reichenbach and the return. It opens on Watson's preface — follow its links; “To the selected” takes you to the entry's time. Made-up data in a separate space, removed with one button.
onboarding.try.own.title: Start with your own records
onboarding.try.own.body: Name your first Scope — and the first record is already waiting.
onboarding.storage: The data is kept in the browser on this device. A copy can be saved through “Export data”.
firstGroup.title: First Scope
firstGroup.heading: Records can be gathered into Scopes
firstGroup.what: A Scope is a context the records belong to: “Work”, “Health”, “Moving house”. One record can belong to several Scopes.
firstGroup.optional: This is optional: records live without a Scope, and a Scope can be added at any time. Create the first one now if you like.
